VTS Scoring Log

CellVita Research Labs

cellvitaresearchlabs.com · Est. ~2025 · US Manufacturer (claimed) · Scored August 2026

CellVita Research Labs operates a professionally built, publicly accessible site with a dedicated COA index at cellvitaresearchlabs.com/coas listing all 30 products with stated ≥99% HPLC purity. The site claims HPLC, mass spectrometry, and endotoxin screening on every batch through a cGMP-compliant US facility. The gap is that COAs are not downloadable from the index - each product shows a "Request COA" button linking to a contact form. The COA page explicitly states: "documentation is provided per batch on request." No testing laboratory is named. No operating entity, physical address, or policy pages (refund, shipping, or terms) are accessible anywhere on the site - the only links from the footer are to Catalog, Purity & Testing, COAs, Research, and Contact. The site's technology stack suggests a 2025-2026 launch.

Clean public COA index (30 products), HPLC + MS + endotoxin screening claimed, cGMP-compliant US facility stated. All COAs email-on-request only. No lab named, no entity name, no address, no policy pages accessible.

Third-Party Testing Practice 30 Testing scope claimed: HPLC purity (≥99%), mass spectrometry identity confirmation, and endotoxin screening - described as standard for "every lot." cGMP-compliant US manufacturing facility stated. No testing laboratory is named by facility name, address, or credentials. The endotoxin screening claim is a differentiator relative to labs like MZ Biolabs that explicitly exclude it from standard service. Without a named lab, the scope and credibility of the claim cannot be independently evaluated. Partial credit for the specificity of the stated panel. 12/30
Batch Traceability & Verification 20 The COA index at /coas lists all 30 products with "Batch-specific certificate" labels and lot-level documentation stated. Each entry includes the product name and a Request COA link. The structure confirms batch-level documentation exists. However, no batch codes, lot numbers, or sample COA documents are accessible publicly - the index is a catalog of what's available on request, not a browseable archive. Partial credit for the structured batch documentation claim and the publicly accessible index; deduction for the request-only access model. 9/20
COA Accessibility 15 COAs are provided per batch on request via a contact form at /contact?topic=coa. The COA page explicitly states: "Because each certificate is tied to a specific production lot, documentation is provided per batch on request." This is email-on-request access, which scores minimally under VTS methodology. The COA index itself is publicly accessible and well-organized, but the index is a menu, not a library. Minimal credit for the stated availability. 3/15
COA Completeness 15 Claimed panel: HPLC purity, mass spectrometry identity, and endotoxin screening. Partial credit for the specificity of the claimed scope, with deduction for inability to verify. 8/15

Community Signal
Independent Test Results
No community-commissioned independent test results identified in public forums as of August 2026. No presence in Finnrick or other major independent testing datasets at time of scoring. This field will be updated as independently sourced results are published.
Community Experience
No Trustpilot profile identified at time of scoring. Very limited community discussion in public forums. The site's professional design and structured COA index suggest operational intent, but insufficient community data exists to characterize buyer experience.
Scoring Notes
The site's architecture is ahead of its disclosure
The COA index at /coas is one of the cleaner catalog-level documentation structures reviewed - 30 products listed with stated purity, testing scope, and individual COA request links. The site design and the specificity of the testing claims (HPLC + MS + endotoxin screening) indicate a vendor that understands what documentation should look like. The gap is that the architecture stops at the surface: COAs are on request, the lab is unnamed, and no operator is identifiable. The infrastructure is in place for a much higher score - the operator transparency and public COA delivery are the missing pieces.
Absence of policy pages is the sharpest single gap
CellVita is the only vendor in the VTS catalog with no identifiable refund policy, shipping policy, terms of service, or privacy policy accessible at time of scoring. A researcher who has a problem with an order has no publicly stated recourse. This is a meaningful buyer risk that the otherwise professional site presentation does not address.
Sources: cellvitaresearchlabs.com (homepage, /coas, /purity-testing, /catalog, /contact). VTS measures process transparency from publicly available materials only. It is not a certification of product safety, purity, or efficacy. PeptideClear has no affiliate, referral, or commercial relationship with CellVita Research Labs. Scored August 2026 - reviewed on a rolling basis as vendor practices change.
